title: Bill of Rights, Amendment I: religion, speech, press, assembly, petition
summary: The National Archives transcription of Amendment I, ratified 15 December 1791, is the text this card reports.
body: The National Archives transcription of the Bill of Rights gives Amendment I, ratified on 15 December 1791. The following is a close rendering in modern spelling, not a character-for-character copy of the enrolled capitalisation: Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof, or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition the government for a redress of grievances. The Archives page keeps the capitalisation of the enrolled resolution. This card reports the operative rule. It does not collect later cases that have read the sentence.

sources.title: The Bill of Rights: A Transcription
sources.author: U.S. National Archives
sources.note: Transcription opened 2026-11-18. The card quotes the transcript. It does not add a later political reading unless a second opened page says it.

said_by: United States Congress and the ratifying states
